experiments.name: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments – Burning Rate Emulator
experiments.hardware: ACME hardware in Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR)
experiments.pis: J. Quintiere, J. de Ris, P. Sunderland, D. Stocker
experiments.goal: Figure out how solid and liquid materials burn in still microgravity by simulating them with gas on a porous burner, and map when these fires start and stop in space-like atmospheres.
experiments.flame_3d: Expected dome/hemispherical flame sitting on a flat porous disk burner (25 or 50 mm diameter) in still air. Model: half-ellipsoid shell over a disk; slow growth/shrink as burner heats; blue-to-faint yellow colour depending on fuel (CH4 vs C2H4).
experiments.oxygen: Exploration atmospheres: 21% O2 @ 14.7 psia; 26.5% @ 10.2 psia; 34% @ 8.2 psia. O2/CO2 ambients also desired.
experiments.flow: Quiescent (no forced airflow) – deliberately mimics a spacecraft with ventilation shut off.
experiments.fuel: CH4/N2 and C2H4/N2 mixtures through 25 mm and 50 mm porous circular burners, chosen to emulate heat of combustion, heat of gasification and smoke point of real solids (e.g. PMMA, nylon).
experiments.variables: Fuel mixture, fuel flow rate (stepped down to find extinction), burner size, ambient O2 %, pressure, diluent (N2 vs CO2). Burner surface temperature and heat flux drift during each test, so one test sweeps many conditions.
experiments.sensors: Burner heat-flux sensor and surface temperature; flame imaging; flow-rate and chamber condition logging (ACME/CIR suite).
experiments.findings: Quasi-steady burning matching materials like PMMA and nylon was observed with NO airflow in elevated-O2 atmospheres, whereas the same flames at 21% O2 self-extinguished quickly. Suggests NASA's cone-calorimeter Test 2 could predict microgravity flammability.
experiments.moon: Directly tests the 26.5–34% O2, reduced-pressure atmospheres expected for Moon Base and rovers; shows 'turn off the fans' may not extinguish fires there.

experiments.name: Flame Extinguishment Experiment
experiments.hardware: Multi-user Droplet Combustion Apparatus (MDCA) in CIR
experiments.pis: F. Williams, B. Shaw, M. Hicks, V. Nayagam, M. Choi, F. Dryer, D. Dietrich
experiments.goal: Find out when liquid fuels catch fire in microgravity, test how well different gases put them out, and determine the lowest oxygen levels needed to keep them burning at various pressures.
experiments.flame_3d: Spherical diffusion flame surrounding a free or fibre-tethered droplet (~3 mm and up); flame radius several times the droplet; may leave a soot shell; shrinks to extinction. Model: concentric spheres (droplet + flame shell), radius vs time from burn-rate curve.
experiments.oxygen: Ambient O2 mole fraction stepped down until no ignition (finds LOI); suppressant (CO2, He, SF6) diluted atmospheres.
experiments.flow: Mostly quiescent; some tests impose a slow, sub-buoyant flow by translating the droplet; free droplets may drift slowly.
experiments.fuel: Liquid fuel droplets, free-floating or fibre-supported, ~3 mm initial diameter and larger.
experiments.variables: Initial droplet size, ambient O2 mole fraction, pressure, suppressant type/concentration, drift/translation velocity.
experiments.sensors: Measurements targeted (per PSI objectives): droplet burning rate, flame extinction, heat radiation, soot levels and temperature profiles, using the MDCA diagnostics.
experiments.findings: Test procedure builds Limiting-Oxygen-Index vs pressure diagrams and suppressant-efficacy data. Cool flames observed in FLEX became the basis of follow-on studies (CFI, PSI-142, PSI-117).
experiments.moon: Suppressant efficacy and LOI data are the baseline for choosing extinguishing agents in sealed habitats.
experiments.related: PSI-68 FLEX-2, PSI-39 CFI, PSI-142, PSI-117

experiments.name: Burning and Suppression of Solids – II
experiments.hardware: Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG), SPICE fan-driven flow duct
experiments.pis: P. Ferkul, C. Fernandez-Pello, F. Miller, J. T'ien, S. Bhattacharjee
experiments.goal: Observe how solid fuels ignite and burn in slow airflows to understand how Earth-based fire safety tests compare to actual fire behavior in microgravity.
experiments.flame_3d: Flames over solids burn as 'oval balls' rather than upward cones (PSI description). Model: ellipsoid wrapped around a slab, rod or spherical-section sample, elongated downstream in concurrent flow, compact at the leading edge in opposed flow.
experiments.oxygen: Below 21% – O2 reduced by adding nitrogen (vitiation) to find limits.
experiments.flow: Forced flow up to 40 cm/s; opposed or concurrent direction.
experiments.fuel: Thick, realistic samples: slabs, cylinders/rods, spherical sections, films, fabric sheets (e.g. PMMA).
experiments.variables: Flow speed and direction, ambient O2 concentration, sample geometry and material.
experiments.sensors: Video imaging of flame appearance, growth and spread rate (MSG cameras).
experiments.findings: Tests the hypothesis that ventilated materials burn as well or better in µg than in 1g, meaning 1g upward-burn screening may not be conservative for space.
experiments.moon: Low-speed flows (cabin ventilation) are the dominant oxidizer supply in µg; key for habitat airflow design.

experiments.name: Flame Extinguishment Experiment – 2
experiments.pis: F. Williams, F. Dryer, B. Shaw, M. Choi, V. Nayagam, T. Avedisian, D. Dietrich, M. Hicks
experiments.goal: Expand previous liquid fuel tests to use realistic fuels and conditions, focusing on how mixed-fuel droplets burn, create soot, interact with each other, and eventually extinguish.
experiments.flame_3d: Spherical droplet flame with soot shell; binary droplet arrays give merged/peanut-shaped flames. Translating droplets give slightly upstream-compressed spheres.
experiments.oxygen: O2 mole fraction 0.10 – 0.40 (balance diluent) – covers Moon-base range.
experiments.flow: Quiescent or droplet translation (controlled velocity and acceleration).
experiments.fuel: Pure and bi-component liquid fuel droplets (single and binary linear arrays).
experiments.variables: Fuel type, ambient gas composition, pressure, initial droplet diameter, translation velocity/acceleration, droplet spacing in arrays.
experiments.sensors: Colour camera video (near-real-time), high-speed photography of flame evolution, chamber pressure and temperature.
experiments.findings: Benchmark data to validate Navier–Stokes droplet-combustion models including radiative vs diffusive extinction transitions.
experiments.moon: O2 range up to 40% overlaps expected habitat atmospheres.

experiments.name: Burning and Suppression of Solids
experiments.hardware: MSG, SPICE fan-driven flow duct (76 × 76 mm)
experiments.pis: P. Ferkul, F. Takahashi, J. T'ien, S. Olson
experiments.goal: Test thick, realistic materials to compare Earth-based fire tests with true microgravity burning, and evaluate how effectively nitrogen gas puts out these fires.
experiments.flame_3d: Flame spreading along a fabric strip, sphere or cylinder; concurrent flow gives a long trailing flame, opposed flow a short blue leading edge. Model: deformable sheet flame on a plane with spread-rate-driven front.
experiments.oxygen: Cabin air with N2 added as suppressant.
experiments.flow: Variable-speed fan, up to 40 cm/s; opposed or concurrent.
experiments.fuel: SIBAL fabric (75% cotton / 25% fiberglass), Nomex, Ultem; flat strips, spheres, cylinders. Kanthal hot-wire igniter.
experiments.variables: Flow speed and direction, sample material and shape, preheating, N2 suppression.
experiments.sensors: Top and edge-view video: flame size, shape, colour, spread rate and quenching.
experiments.findings: Supports the hypothesis that adequately ventilated materials burn as well as or better than in 1g; gives radiative-emission data used to extend cone-calorimeter (Test 2) results.
experiments.moon: Same flow-duct approach transferable to partial-g airflow studies; N2 suppression links to current ISS practice.

experiments.name: Spacecraft Fire Experiment – II
experiments.hardware: Saffire flow duct in Cygnus pressurized module
experiments.pis: D. Urban, G. Ruff
experiments.goal: Measure how quickly large fires spread on actual spacecraft materials in low gravity, and compare the results to standard Earth-based safety tests.
experiments.flame_3d: Flame fronts spreading across nine 5 × 29 cm sample strips in a flow duct; concurrent = elongated flame downstream, opposed = narrow front. Model: textured planes with animated burn front.
experiments.oxygen: Spacecraft cabin air (O2 and CO2 mole fractions measured).
experiments.flow: 20 or 30 cm/s, concurrent or opposed depending on sample.
experiments.fuel: SIBAL, silicone, structured PMMA, flat PMMA, PMMA with Nomex.
experiments.variables: Sample material, flow speed (20/30 cm/s), flow direction.
experiments.sensors: 2 cameras, thermocouples (flow, flame, plume temperature), 2 radiometers, solid-state pressure, CO2 and O2 sensors, 2 anemometers.
experiments.findings: Determines µg flammability limits for several spacecraft materials and checks NASA's material-selection criteria at realistic scale without risking crew.
experiments.moon: Only large-scale data on real cabin materials; key validation for habitat fire models.

experiments.name: ACME – Cool Flames Investigation with Gases
experiments.sub: Flames of gaseous fuels (cool diffusion flames)
experiments.pis: P. Sunderland, R. Axelbaum, F. Williams, D. Stocker
experiments.goal: Discover the right conditions to create steady, low-temperature "cool flames" using different gases on a spherical burner, and use the data to verify computer combustion models.
experiments.flame_3d: Spherical flame around a porous sphere burner. In the high-O2 tests, O2/N2 (up to 85% O2) flows OUT of the burner into a fuel/N2 chamber, giving an inside-out (inverse) flame. Cool flames are very faint; render as a translucent, low-luminosity shell.
experiments.oxygen: Up to 85% O2 issuing from the burner (highest O2 in any PSI microgravity test).
experiments.flow: Burner outflow only (no ambient flow); flow rate varied.
experiments.fuel: Propane, n-butane, n-pentane (ethane also listed in keywords), diluted with N2.
experiments.variables: Fuel, normal vs inverse configuration, stoichiometric mixture fraction Zst, adiabatic flame temperature, flow rate, pressure, dilution.
experiments.sensors: Cameras (incl. intensified video), radiometers, photomultiplier tubes, thermocouples.
experiments.findings: Tests whether reducing flow extinguishes a cool flame while increasing it triggers a hot flame, with possible hot/cool oscillation.
experiments.moon: Highest-oxygen microgravity combustion data available – closest analogue to O2-enriched habitat atmospheres.

experiments.name: ACME – Electric-Field Effects on Laminar Diffusion Flames
experiments.hardware: ACME hardware in CIR (coflow & gas-jet burners, copper mesh electrode)
experiments.pis: D. Dunn-Rankin, D. Stocker, A. Chien
experiments.goal: Study how applying an electric field affects a flame's shape, stability, and soot production, using the electricity to mimic the effects of gravity.
experiments.flame_3d: Axisymmetric jet flame from a small burner, with a flat circular mesh electrode above. The field drives an ion wind that stretches or flattens the flame toward/away from the mesh – a body force that can mimic partial gravity. Model: cylinder-capped flame whose height/tip curvature is driven by a 'g-equivalent' slider.
experiments.oxygen: Weak synthetic-air coflow (21% O2 nominal); fuel diluted with N2.
experiments.flow: Gas jet with or without weak air coflow (same coflow burner as CLD).
experiments.fuel: Methane and ethylene, diluted with N2 (e.g. 40–100% CH4, 80% C2H4 per test table).
experiments.variables: Voltage (up to 10 kV), mesh polarity, fuel and dilution, fuel flow rate, coflow velocity. 33 test days in experimental table.
experiments.sensors: Voltage–current (ion current) curves, high-resolution cameras (shape, luminosity, soot), spectral filtered imaging (chemiluminescence, soot volume fraction), thermopiles (radiant emission).
experiments.findings: Hypothesis: electric fields let researchers manipulate flame stability, soot and dynamics through ion-driven convection and chemi-ionization, giving a controllable stand-in for buoyancy.
experiments.moon: Only PSI dataset that mimics partial gravity (via electric body force); can help interpolate between 0 g and 1 g for Moon (0.16 g) and Mars (0.38 g).

experiments.name: Concurrent Flame Spread Modeling using Flamelet Generated Manifolds with Comparison to BASS (Two-Color Tomography)
experiments.pis: P. DesJardin, D. Urban
experiments.goal: Create and verify a computer model that predicts how fires spread across solid materials in space.
experiments.flame_3d: Best method for real 3D shapes: two-colour tomography on BASS DSLR images reconstructs 3D soot and temperature fields over PMMA sheets, spheres, rods and wax cylinders. The PSI entry is only 9.47 KB, so reconstructions are likely in the publications/final report; reproduce the method on BASS imagery.
experiments.oxygen: As in BASS/BASS-II cases.
experiments.flow: As in BASS/BASS-II (concurrent flow).
experiments.fuel: PMMA flat sheets, spheres, rods; wax cylinders.
experiments.variables: Sample geometry, model parameters; validated on flame geometry, temperature, soot volume fraction, spread rate.
experiments.sensors: Computational; post-processed BASS DSLR imagery (two-colour pyrometry/tomography).
experiments.findings: Aims to reproduce the 'Goldilocks' flammability zone (flames survive only in a middle range of flow speeds) reported by Olson and Ferkul.
experiments.moon: Provides a predictive model for fire scenarios that can be re-run for habitat O2/pressure.

experiments.name: ACME – Flame Design
experiments.pis: R. Axelbaum, P. Sunderland, D. Urban, D. Stocker, S. Frolov
experiments.goal: Study round flames to see when they produce soot and when they go out under various conditions, and determine if a perfectly steady round flame can exist.
experiments.flame_3d: Spherical diffusion flame around a porous sphere; normal (fuel out) or inverse (O2 out). Yellow sooty inner region for C2H4, blue soot-free for CH4/high Zst. Model: sphere with radial colour gradient; radius from flow rate.
experiments.oxygen: Varied via oxidizer stream and stoichiometric mixture fraction (Zst); inverse flames issue oxidizer from the burner.
experiments.flow: Burner outflow only; flow rate varied.
experiments.fuel: Ethylene and methane with N2 or CO2 inert.
experiments.variables: Flow rate, Zst, amount and type of inert, pressure, normal vs inverse direction.
experiments.sensors: Cameras, radiometers, photomultiplier tubes, thermocouples.
experiments.findings: Hypothesis: µg spherical diffusion flames extinguish when peak temperature first drops below ~1130 K; steady-state spherical flames are possible (publications report long-duration ISS observations).
experiments.moon: Shows how oxygen placement and dilution control soot and radiative extinction – relevant to O2-enriched cabins.

experiments.name: Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment – Reflight
experiments.hardware: Comparative Soot Diagnostic hardware in MSG
experiments.pis: D. Urban, Z. Yuan, J. Yang, T. Cleary, G. Mulholland, C. Fortenberry
experiments.goal: Measure the size of smoke particles in low gravity to understand how smoke forms and moves, helping to build better smoke detectors for spacecraft.
experiments.flame_3d: No flame – heated/pyrolyzing sample producing a smoke plume. Model: particle system (aerosol cloud) that stays near the source in µg.
experiments.oxygen: Cabin air
experiments.flow: Controlled flow, including new 'no-flow during heating' condition.
experiments.fuel: Overheated spacecraft materials; Pyrell intumescent foam added (replacing DBP).
experiments.variables: Material, heating temperature (higher than SAME), flow vs no-flow, aging time. 66 test points.
experiments.sensors: M-pass (new GRC instrument), DustTrak, ionization smoke detector, thermal precipitators.
experiments.findings: Hypothesis: µg smoke particles are larger (fewer per mass), which can stop some detectors from alarming; post-flight tests validated the lognormal size-distribution assumption.
experiments.moon: Detector selection for habitats depends on µg/partial-g smoke size.

experiments.name: Spacecraft Fire Safety Experiment – I
experiments.pis: D. Urban
experiments.goal: Find out how fast a large fire spreads in microgravity on a single large sheet of fabric and compare it to standard Earth-based fire safety tests.
experiments.flame_3d: Flame spreading over a single large 0.94 × 0.40 m fabric sheet in a flow duct. Model: large plane with animated flame front and plume.
experiments.oxygen: Cabin air (O2 and CO2 tracked).
experiments.flow: 20 cm/s
experiments.fuel: SIBAL (75% cotton / 25% fiberglass), 0.94 m × 0.4 m.
experiments.variables: Single large-sample burn (limited variation).
experiments.sensors: 2 cameras, thermocouples, 2 radiometers, pressure/CO2/O2 sensors, 2 anemometers.
experiments.findings: A realistic-scale fire studied safely on an uncrewed vehicle: flame growth data and how µg and limited O2 affect flame size.
experiments.moon: Large-scale realism; baseline for cabin O2 depletion and CO2 rise during a fire.

experiments.name: Spacecraft Fire Experiment – III
experiments.pis: D. Urban
experiments.goal: Similar to Saffire-I, this tests how fast large fires grow in microgravity compared to Earth tests, but introduces faster airflows.
experiments.flame_3d: Large SIBAL sheet with spreading flame front; concurrent or opposed flow.
experiments.oxygen: Cabin air (O2 and CO2 tracked).
experiments.flow: 30 cm/s (vs 20 cm/s in Saffire-I), concurrent or opposed.
experiments.fuel: SIBAL fabric.
experiments.variables: Flow speed and direction (compared with Saffire-I).
experiments.sensors: 2 cameras, thermocouples, 2 radiometers, pressure/CO2/O2 sensors, 2 anemometers.
experiments.findings: Adds the flow-speed effect on large-scale flame growth.
experiments.moon: Same as Saffire-I.

experiments.name: ACME – Coflow Laminar Diffusion Flame
experiments.pis: M. Long, M. Smooke, D. Stocker
experiments.goal: Study the shape, temperature, soot levels, and extinction points of weak gas flames under different airflow speeds and fuel mixtures.
experiments.flame_3d: Axisymmetric coflow jet flame: in µg it is wider, longer and round-tipped (no teardrop); dilute flames lift off the burner rim. Model: surface of revolution from a measured flame-height profile, base offset = lift-off height.
experiments.oxygen: Air coflow (21% O2); fuel diluted with N2.
experiments.flow: Coflow air velocity varied; fuel velocity varied.
experiments.fuel: Methane (25–40% in N2 per test table) and ethylene.
experiments.variables: Fuel type, fuel dilution, fuel and coflow velocity. 33 test days in experimental table.
experiments.sensors: OH* and CH* chemiluminescence imaging, soot luminosity, laser extinction (soot volume fraction), thin-filament pyrometry (gas temperature).
experiments.findings: Benchmark data to improve soot sub-models across dilute to heavily sooting flames.
experiments.moon: Validated soot models feed radiative heat-transfer predictions in fire models.

experiments.name: Smoke and Aerosol Measurement Experiment
experiments.hardware: Comparative Soot Diagnostic hardware in MSG
experiments.pis: D. Urban, G. Mulholland, T. Cleary, J. Yang, C. Fortenberry
experiments.goal: Measure smoke particle sizes in microgravity under various conditions to help create a computer program that predicts how smoke droplets grow.
experiments.flame_3d: No flame – smoke from overheated material. Model: aerosol cloud.
experiments.oxygen: Cabin air
experiments.flow: Controlled flow field
experiments.fuel: Overheated spacecraft materials (incl. DBP samples).
experiments.variables: Sample temperature, flow field, particle aging time, igniter heating time (15–60 s).
experiments.sensors: Two smoke detectors, thermophoretic samplers (TEM analysis post-flight), mass-loss weighing, video.
experiments.findings: TEM grids came back contaminated (motivating SAME-R); detector response was still determined from the video record.
experiments.moon: Baseline for smoke-detector design in habitats.

experiments.name: Utilization of SAME Data for Advanced Modeling of Smoke Generation in Micro-Gravity
experiments.pis: S. Garrick, M. Hicks
experiments.goal: Use computer simulations to figure out exactly how the lack of gravity changes the way smoke grows and moves.
experiments.flame_3d: No flame – simulated buoyant vs non-buoyant smoke wakes downstream of a hot vapour source.
experiments.oxygen: N/A (DBP pyrolysis vapour)
experiments.flow: Two low cross-flow speeds
experiments.fuel: Dibutyl phthalate (DBP) vapour, SAME-like geometry.
experiments.variables: Gravity (0 vs 1 g), cross-flow speed; thermophoresis and settling effects.
experiments.sensors: Computational (DNS).
experiments.findings: Hypothesis: without buoyancy, mixing and heat transfer drop, changing particle growth and smoke composition.
experiments.moon: Simulation approach can be re-run at lunar/Martian g.

experiments.name: Smoke Point In Co-flow Experiment
experiments.hardware: MSG with SPICE fan-driven flow duct
experiments.pis: D. Urban, P. Sunderland
experiments.goal: Determine the exact point at which gas flames start producing smoke in microgravity, and see how burner size and airflow affect the flame's length and soot.
experiments.flame_3d: Small jet flame from a needle burner in coflow; at the smoke point the tip opens and emits soot. Model: elongated flame with an 'open tip' particle emitter.
experiments.oxygen: Air coflow (21% O2)
experiments.flow: Coflow 5.4 – 65 cm/s
experiments.fuel: Methane, ethylene, propane, propylene and mixtures; burner diameters 0.41, 0.76, 1.6 mm.
experiments.variables: Fuel, burner diameter, coflow velocity, fuel flow rate (increased to reach smoke point). 526 flames.
experiments.sensors: Still and video cameras, radiative heat-loss measurement, coflow velocity distribution.
experiments.findings: Hypothesis: without gravity-driven transport, smoke-point properties differ significantly from 1g. The images were later used to derive soot temperature and volume fraction (PSI-60).
experiments.moon: Sooting propensity governs radiation and smoke load for detectors.

experiments.name: ACME – Structure and Response of Spherical Diffusion Flames
experiments.pis: C. K. Law, S. Tse, D. Stocker
experiments.goal: Observe how round flames change over time, when they naturally put themselves out, and how they sometimes pulse or flicker before extinguishing.
experiments.flame_3d: Expanding spherical flame on a porous sphere burner; can pulsate (radius oscillation) near extinction. Model: sphere with time-varying radius.
experiments.oxygen: Oxidizing ambient; fuel/diluent ratio varied.
experiments.flow: Burner outflow only; flow rate varied.
experiments.fuel: H2/CH4/diluent (soot-free) and C2H4/diluent (sooty); diluents N2, He, CO2.
experiments.variables: Fuel/diluent ratio, diluent type, flow rate (Damköhler number).
experiments.sensors: Spectrally resolved images, flame and burner temperatures, radiative flux, flow rates, ambient T/P, acceleration levels.
experiments.findings: Rigorous test of detailed chemistry/transport/radiation models; transient extinction limits.
experiments.moon: Radiative-extinction limits inform when large µg flames self-extinguish.

experiments.name: Cool Flames Investigation
experiments.pis: F. Williams, F. Dryer, T. Farouk, V. Nayagam, D. Dietrich
experiments.goal: Investigate how liquid fuel droplets burn at unusually low temperatures ("cool flames") under different pressures and sizes.
experiments.flame_3d: Faint spherical cool flame around a tethered droplet; transitions between hot and cool. Model: translucent sphere with low emissive intensity.
experiments.oxygen: O2 with N2 and He diluents.
experiments.flow: Quiescent
experiments.fuel: n-dodecane, farnesane, n-dodecane/iso-dodecane droplets (needle-suspended or SiC-fibre tethered).
experiments.variables: Fuel, pressure, He dilution, droplet size.
experiments.sensors: B&W camera (droplet size), UV camera (OH* emission, flame size), narrow- and wide-band radiometers.
experiments.findings: Hypothesis: µg droplet burning reveals extinction diameters and cool-flame dynamics that cannot be observed on Earth.
experiments.moon: Cool flames can persist after visible flames go out – a hidden re-ignition hazard.

experiments.name: Structure and Liftoff In Combustion Experiment
experiments.hardware: MSG with SPICE fan-driven flow duct
experiments.pis: M. Long, M. Smooke, F. Takahashi, D. Stocker
experiments.goal: Study how gas flames remain stable or detach from their burner in microgravity, and how diluting the fuel changes soot production.
experiments.flame_3d: Coflow jet flame that lifts off the burner as velocity increases. Model: flame body with adjustable lift-off gap.
experiments.oxygen: Air coflow
experiments.flow: Fan-driven coflow, varied
experiments.fuel: Methane, ethylene, N2-diluted mixtures; exchangeable burner tubes.
experiments.variables: Fuel, dilution, burner diameter, coflow velocity. 13 test runs, >4,000 images.
experiments.sensors: High-resolution still camera with sensor data overlaid; flow-rate and temperature sensors.
experiments.findings: Hypothesis: burner diameter, coflow velocity and fuel composition control flame structure and stability, which differ fundamentally from 1g.
experiments.moon: Flame anchoring vs airflow informs how ventilation can blow out or stabilize fires.

experiments.name: Computational and Experimental Analysis of SPICE Data Sets
experiments.pis: M. Smooke, M. Long, D. Dietrich
experiments.goal: Analyze over 1,600 flame images to calculate soot temperatures and amounts, comparing microgravity results with Earth-based predictions.
experiments.flame_3d: Measured 2D temperature/soot fields of SPICE flames (colour-ratio pyrometry) – usable as textures on an axisymmetric flame model (PSI entry is only 7.56 KB, so fields are probably in the publications).
experiments.oxygen: As SPICE
experiments.flow: As SPICE
experiments.fuel: As SPICE; Yale and ACME burner configurations simulated.
experiments.variables: Gravity, radiation/scattering, boundary conditions, model parameters.
experiments.sensors: Image processing of raw Nikon NEF files; computational soot models.
experiments.findings: Hypothesis: µg flames are longer, more diffuse, cooler and sootier.
experiments.moon: Validated soot models for radiation in habitat fire models.

experiments.name: Dust and Aerosol Measurement Feasibility Test
experiments.pis: D. Urban, C. Fortenberry
experiments.goal: Confirm that a specific particle-counting device functions properly in microgravity so it can be used in later smoke detection tests.
experiments.flame_3d: No flame – dust aerosol in Mylar bags.
experiments.oxygen: N/A
experiments.flow: N/A
experiments.fuel: Arizona Red Dust (ARD) aerosolized with GN2 in 15 L Mylar bags.
experiments.variables: Aerosol standard and filtering.
experiments.sensors: Modified TSI P-Trak (capillary isopropanol recycling) vs DustTrak control.
experiments.findings: Same instrument used for smoke in SAME and for dust here; relevant to lunar dust vs smoke false alarms.
experiments.moon: Lunar dust could confuse smoke detectors – this data is a starting point.

experiments.name: Quantitative Studies of Cool Flame Transitions at Radiation/Stretch Extinction Using Counterflow Flames
experiments.pis: Y. Ju, C. Reuter, D. Dietrich
experiments.goal: Use past data and ground-lab experiments to map out exactly when and how low-temperature "cool flames" can survive under various conditions.
experiments.flame_3d: Flat counterflow flame (1D). Model: thin disk between opposed jets.
experiments.oxygen: Oxygen concentration effects on extinction studied (FLEX conditions).
experiments.flow: Counterflow strain rate
experiments.fuel: n-heptane/air, dimethyl ether (DME).
experiments.variables: O2 concentration, dilution, pressure, strain rate.
experiments.sensors: Ground lab diagnostics + three numerical schemes.
experiments.findings: Links hot-flame and cool-flame flammability/extinction limits.
experiments.moon: Explains when a 'put-out' fire may continue as a cool flame.

experiments.name: Effect of External Thermo-Convective Perturbation on Cool Flame Dynamics: Multidimensional CFD
experiments.pis: T. Farouk, M. Hicks
experiments.goal: Use 3D computer simulations and past data to measure how heat and slight air movements cause droplet "cool flames" to ignite, flicker, and go out.
experiments.flame_3d: 3D CFD model of droplet cool flames (1–4 mm and ~0.5 mm droplets). If field outputs are in the 67.54 MB data package, they can drive a volumetric 3D viewer.
experiments.oxygen: Ambient composition swept, incl. ozone-assisted cases.
experiments.flow: Imposed convection (mimics drift), heat flux, or both.
experiments.fuel: n-alkane droplets.
experiments.variables: Forcing amplitude/frequency, droplet size, ambient composition, pressure.
experiments.sensors: Computational, validated against FLEX.
experiments.findings: Built stability maps for cool-flame onset, persistence and quenching, reconciled with FLEX observations.
experiments.moon: Shows small residual airflows decide whether cool flames survive.
